How to use the ratio
The gold-to-silver ratio compresses two prices into a single number. It's most
useful as a
relative-value signal
— when the ratio is far above
its long-term mean, silver is comparatively cheap; when it's far below, gold is
comparatively cheap.
Below 50:1
— silver expensive relative to gold. Historically rare.
50:1 – 70:1
— neutral band. Most of the 20th century lived here.
70:1 – 85:1
— silver getting cheap. Many investors lean toward silver here.
Above 85:1
— extreme territory. 2020 hit 124:1 during liquidity panic.
Mean reversion is the lesson, not market timing. Extreme readings tend to revert
over multi-year windows — but the "wait" can be years, and you'll need the patience
to hold through volatility.
